newsitem.title: USA: DSP Group rises on analysts comments.
newsitem.headline: DSP Group rises on analysts comments.

text.p: Shares of DSP Group Inc, a maker of digital signal proceessing chips, rose on Monday after Smith Barney initiated it with a rating of buy.
DSP has distinguished itself as one of the premier players in the market, Smith Barney analyst Elliot Prince said.

Digital signal processors chips are designed to manipulate real-world data which have been converted into compressed digital form. The technology is used in digital wireless products and is incorporated into the handsets and bases.
Prince set a 6- to 12-month price target of $26 a share. He said he sees fiscal year 1997 earnings at $0.96 per share and fiscal 1998 earnings at $1.47 a share.
Prince said that more than 25 companies have licensed DSP's technology and are developing proprietary chips that embed DSP's technology.
"As these chips begin to sell, DSP Group will garner significant, high-margin royalty revenues," Prince said.
DSP has also been actively licensing its audio compression technology to companies like Microsoft Corp, 3Com Corp's U.S. Robotics unit and Intel Corp.
Shares of DSP rose 1-1/8 to 21-1/4 on Monday.
